tooltip.title: Overview of Treatment Types for Pruritus
tooltip.markdown: The management of chronic pruritus involves a multimodal approach, combining non-pharmacologic strategies, topical agents, systemic medications, and procedural therapies.

tooltip.title: Foundational & Topical Therapies
tooltip.markdown: First-line approaches for managing itch, especially when localized or associated with dry/inflamed skin.

tooltip.title: Skincare and Barrier Repair
tooltip.markdown: The cornerstone of management. Includes gentle cleansing, trigger avoidance, and frequent use of moisturizers to restore skin barrier function.

tooltip.title: Topical Anti-inflammatories
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Corticosteroids:** Mainstay for itch associated with inflammatory dermatoses (eg, eczema).
-   **Calcineurin Inhibitors:** Tacrolimus and pimecrolimus are steroid-sparing alternatives for sensitive areas.

tooltip.title: Topical Neuromodulators
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Counter-irritants:** Menthol and camphor provide a cooling sensation.
-   **Anesthetics:** Pramoxine and lidocaine provide temporary relief.
-   **Capsaicin:** Depletes neuropeptides from nerve endings; effective for neuropathic itch but causes initial burning.

tooltip.title: Systemic (Oral/Injectable) Therapies
tooltip.markdown: Used for generalized, severe, or refractory pruritus that does not respond to topical measures.

tooltip.title: Antihistamines
tooltip.markdown: Highly effective for histaminergic itch (e.g., urticaria). Limited efficacy in most chronic itch, but sedating first-generation agents can be useful for nocturnal itch.

tooltip.title: Neuromodulators
tooltip.markdown:
A mainstay for neuropathic itch, uremic pruritus, and CPUO.

-   **Gabapentinoids:** Gabapentin and pregabalin.
-   **Antidepressants:** SSRIs (sertraline) and Tricyclics (doxepin) have antipruritic effects.

tooltip.title: Immunomodulators
tooltip.markdown: Used for severe inflammatory itch. Includes methotrexate, cyclosporine, and targeted biologics like Dupilumab (anti-IL-4/13).

tooltip.title: Opioid Modulators
tooltip.markdown: Target the opioid system imbalance in chronic itch. Includes μ-opioid antagonists (naltrexone) and κ-opioid agonists (difelikefalin).
